questions.question: What are routes in Rails and how do you write them?
questions.title: Rails Routes Basics
questions.direct_answer: Routes map URLs to controller actions in config/routes.rb — they're the app's entry point. The forms: get '/about', to: 'pages#about' (a single route); resources :posts (the 7 REST routes); root to: 'posts#index' (the homepage). resources :posts generates GET /posts (index), POST /posts (create), GET /posts/:id (show), PATCH /posts/:id (update), DELETE /posts/:id (destroy), plus new/edit, and path helpers (posts_path, post_path(id)). Nested: resources :posts do resources :comments end gives /posts/:post_id/comments. Check your routes with rails routes (lists every route + helper). Routes are how a URL becomes a controller action.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know routes live in config/routes.rb, the forms (root, get, resources), and that resources :posts gives the 7 routes + helpers.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Hand-writing the 7 routes when resources :posts generates them, or forgetting root (no homepage).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Routes map URLs to actions in config/routes.rb: root, get 'x', to: 'y#z', resources :posts (7 routes + helpers). Check with rails routes.

sections.title: URLs Become Actions
sections.content: Routes map URLs to controller actions in config slash routes.rb — they're the app's entry point. The forms: get slash about, to pages hash about (a single route); resources posts (the 7 REST routes); root to posts index (the homepage). resources posts generates GET slash posts (index), POST slash posts (create), GET slash posts slash id (show), PATCH slash posts slash id (update), DELETE slash posts slash id (destroy), plus new and edit, and path helpers (posts_path, post_path of id). Nested: resources posts do resources comments end gives slash posts slash post_id slash comments. Check your routes with rails routes (lists every route and helper). Routes are how a URL becomes a controller action.

sections.title: routes.rb
sections.content:
root, get, resources :posts (7 routes + helpers). Check with rails routes.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  R[root to: 'posts#index'] --> G[get '/about', to: 'pages#about']
  G --> Rs[resources :posts -> 7 routes]
  Rs --> N[nested: resources :comments]
```

sections.title: Routes
sections.content:
```ruby
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
  root to: 'posts#index'                # GET / -> PostsController#index

  get '/about', to: 'pages#about'        # a single route

  resources :posts                       # the 7 REST routes + helpers
  #   GET    /posts        -> index      posts_path
  #   POST   /posts        -> create     posts_path
  #   GET    /posts/:id    -> show       post_path(@post)
  #   PATCH  /posts/:id    -> update     post_path(@post)
  #   DELETE /posts/:id    -> destroy    post_path(@post)
  #   GET    /posts/new    -> new        new_post_path
  #   GET    /posts/:id/edit -> edit     edit_post_path(@post)

  # Nested resource:
  resources :posts do
    resources :comments                  # /posts/:post_id/comments
  end

  # API-only namespacing:
  namespace :api do
    resources :posts                     # /api/posts -> Api::PostsController
  end
end

# List every route + its helper:  rails routes
```

sections.content: Routes map URLs to controller actions in config slash routes.rb — they're the app's entry point. The forms: get slash about, to pages hash about (a single route); resources posts (the 7 REST routes); root to posts index (the homepage). resources posts generates GET slash posts (index), POST slash posts (create), GET slash posts slash id (show), PATCH slash posts slash id (update), DELETE slash posts slash id (destroy), plus new and edit, and path helpers (posts_path, post_path of id). Nested: resources posts do resources comments end gives slash posts slash post_id slash comments. Check your routes with rails routes (lists every route and helper).
